content.text: In countries like Zimbabwe, where conventional payment platforms like Stripe and PayPal are severely restricted, digital creators face significant challenges in setting up online stores that can accept crypto payments. This is where COREMERCH's infrastructure solutions come in, providing a way for creators to build and deploy their own digital stores with automatic crypto payment processing. This guide will focus on Supabase as the order database for digital stores and how to deploy it today.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The key to COREMERCH's infrastructure is its use of decentralized and open-source technologies, which allow creators to maintain full control over their stores and data. By using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, creators can build a robust and scalable e-commerce platform that is not dependent on any single platform or service. This approach also enables automatic crypto payment processing through NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and has a low fee of 0.5%.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store, you'll need to set up a few key components, including a GitHub or Cloudflare account, a Supabase instance, and a NOWPayments account. You'll also need to have a clear understanding of your store's requirements, including the types of products you'll be selling and the payment options you'll be offering. Additionally, you'll need to ensure that you have a reliable internet connection and a basic understanding of web development principles.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Once you have all the necessary components in place, you can start setting up your payment and delivery pipeline. This involves configuring your Supabase instance to store order data, setting up your NOWPayments account to process crypto payments, and integrating your payment gateway with your store's frontend. You'll also need to configure your store's delivery pipeline, which may involve setting up a file delivery system using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2.
Supabase provides a scalable and secure order database for your digital store.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

With your store's infrastructure in place, you can now go live and start processing transactions. This involves deploying your store to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, configuring your domain settings, and testing your store's functionality. Once you've completed these steps, you can start promoting your store and accepting crypto payments from customers. It's essential to test your store thoroughly to ensure that all components are working as expected.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your store is up and running, you can start thinking about scaling your infrastructure to meet growing demand. This may involve upgrading your Supabase instance, adding more payment options, or optimizing your store's performance for better user experience. You can also consider implementing additional security measures, such as SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, to protect your store from spam and phishing attacks.
